title: MongoDB
overview: MongoDB is the most popular document database: JSON-like BSON documents in collections, a rich query language, and horizontal sharding built in. Flexible schemas make it the default for product catalogs, content platforms, and any app whose data shape evolves fast.

demo.how_to_run: Paste into mongosh, or save as demo.js and run: mongosh < demo.js

consistency: Tunable: single-document ACID; multi-document transactions supported
features: Flexible BSON document model, no fixed schema
Secondary indexes incl. text, geospatial, vector search
Replica sets for HA, sharding for scale
when_to_use: Apps needing flexible schema + rich queries
when_not_to_use: Complex multi-table joins — relational fits better

install.debian_ubuntu: Add the MongoDB apt repo, then: sudo apt install mongodb-org
install.macos: brew tap mongodb/brew && brew install mongodb-community

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Apache CouchDB
overview: CouchDB is the original offline-first document database: JSON documents, MapReduce views, and master-master replication that syncs phones, laptops, and servers. Its HTTP API means any client can talk to it with curl.

demo.code:
# CouchDB speaks HTTP — curl is the demo
curl -X PUT http://admin:secret@localhost:5984/shop
curl -X PUT http://admin:secret@localhost:5984/shop/widget1 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sku":"WIDGET-1","qty":50}'
curl http://admin:secret@localhost:5984/shop/widget1
# Mango query:
curl -X POST http://admin:secret@localhost:5984/shop/_find \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"selector":{"qty":{"$lt":20}}}'
demo.how_to_run: Run the curl commands in order against a local CouchDB

query_language: HTTP REST API, Mango queries, MapReduce views
features: Master-master replication incl. PouchDB browser sync
Pure HTTP/JSON API — no driver needed

install.docker: docker run -d --name couch -p 5984:5984 -e COUCHDB_USER=admin -e COUCHDB_PASSWORD=secret couchdb:3

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Redis
overview: Redis is the in-memory data-structure server the whole industry uses as cache, session store, queue, and realtime backend. Strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, and JSON — all at sub-millisecond speed, with optional persistence.

demo.code:
# redis-cli demo (also pasteable as a file: redis-cli < demo.txt)
HSET product:WIDGET-1 sku WIDGET-1 qty 50
HSET product:GADGET-2 sku GADGET-2 qty 12
HGETALL product:WIDGET-1
ZADD leaderboard 1500 alice 1200 bob
ZREVRANGE leaderboard 0 2 WITHSCORES
XADD orders * sku WIDGET-1 qty 2
demo.how_to_run: redis-cli < demo.txt  (or type each line at the redis-cli prompt)

consistency: Single-master strong; async replicas; Cluster sharding
query_language: Redis commands (text protocol), RediSearch/RediSQL via modules
features: Rich types: hashes, sets, sorted sets, streams, HyperLogLog
Pub/sub, blocking queues, rate limiting primitives
when_not_to_use: Primary system of record without persistence planning

install.macos: brew install redis && brew services start redis

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

title: Amazon DynamoDB
overview: DynamoDB is AWS’s serverless key-value/document database: single-digit-millisecond latency at any scale, on-demand pricing, and zero servers. The price is a strict data-model discipline — design access patterns first, tables second.

demo.code:
# AWS CLI demo (or DynamoDB Local on port 8000)
aws dynamodb put-item --table-name shop \
  --item '{"sku":{"S":"WIDGET-1"},"qty":{"N":"50"}}'
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name shop --key '{"sku":{"S":"WIDGET-1"}}'
aws dynamodb scan --table-name shop \
  --filter-expression "qty < :t" --expression-attribute-values '{":t":{"N":"20"}}'
demo.how_to_run: Run with AWS CLI configured (or point --endpoint-url at DynamoDB Local)

consistency: Eventually consistent reads default; strongly consistent optional; transactions supported
features: Serverless: scales to zero, pay per request
Single-digit ms latency at any throughput
when_to_use: AWS serverless apps needing predictable scale
Key-based access patterns you can design up front
when_not_to_use: Ad-hoc analytics — export to S3/Athena instead

install.aws_cli: aws dynamodb create-table --table-name shop --attribute-definitions AttributeName=sku,AttributeType=S --key-schema AttributeName=sku,KeyType=HASH --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST
install.local: Run DynamoDB Local in Docker for development: amazon/dynamodb-local

provenance: Public record of a real database engine; facts fact-checked against vendor documentation.

features: Masterless: every node equal, no SPOF

title: Apache HBase
overview: HBase is the Hadoop-ecosystem wide-column store modeled on Google Bigtable: sparse tables with billions of rows and millions of columns, strong consistency per row, and coprocessors for in-region computation. The choice for Hadoop-native massive sparse data.

demo.code:
# hbase shell demo
create 'inventory', 'cf'
put 'inventory', 'WIDGET-1', 'cf:qty', '50'
put 'inventory', 'GADGET-2', 'cf:qty', '12'
get 'inventory', 'WIDGET-1'
scan 'inventory', {LIMIT => 10}
# Phoenix SQL skin:
# CREATE TABLE inventory (sku VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY, qty INTEGER);
demo.how_to_run: hbase shell < demo.txt

query_language: HBase shell / Java API / Phoenix SQL skin
features: Billions of rows x millions of columns, sparse
Apache Phoenix adds SQL + secondary indexes
Snapshots, replication, MOB for large objects
when_to_use: Hadoop shops needing random read/write at scale
when_not_to_use: Simple key-value needs — heavier than needed

install.standalone: Download from hbase.apache.org; standalone mode runs on one machine
install.docker: Use a community hbase-standalone image for trials

printf "incr sku:WIDGET-1 5\r\n" | nc localhost 11211

title: FoundationDB
overview: FoundationDB is Apple’s open-sourced ordered key-value store with true multi-key ACID transactions and a layered architecture — document, graph, and SQL layers all run on top. The correctness-obsessed foundation for custom databases.

demo.code:
# pip install fdb  (FoundationDB Python bindings)
import fdb
fdb.api_version(730)
db = fdb.open()

@fdb.transactional
def demo(tr):
    tr[b'shop:WIDGET-1'] = b'50'
    tr[b'shop:GADGET-2'] = b'12'
    for k, v in tr[b'shop:':b'shop;\xff']:
        print(k.decode(), int(v))
demo(db)
demo.how_to_run: python demo.py  (needs local FoundationDB server running)

features: Ordered keys: range scans are fast
when_to_use: Building your own database on a correct core
Workloads needing multi-key transactions at scale
when_not_to_use: You want queries out of the box — add a layer

install.macos: Download the macOS installer from foundationdb.org
